author: Marcus Udén (Codex)
source: historical backfill across repository decision logs, plans, lessons, and sanitized harness evidence

policy.date_rule: Use explicit decision dates first. Never infer a decision date from filesystem modification time.
policy.project_rule: Every record has one primary project tag and optional capability tags.
policy.public_rule: Only sanitized records with sufficient evidence can enter the public profile oracle.
policy.source_rule: Plans, lessons, memory, and incident reports are evidence sources, not automatic public content.

records.title: Classify historical decisions before exporting them
records.context: Historical decisions are distributed across repository documents and harness records.
records.decision: Extract, date, tag, classify, deduplicate, and review candidates before creating recruiter-facing entries.
records.tradeoff: The process is slower than copying documents directly, but it protects chronology, evidence quality, and privacy.
records.redaction_notes: Publish the resulting records, not the source plan.

records.title: Name the operating layer Personal AI Harness
records.context: The system contains memory, agents, automation, reusable workflows, and recursive improvement, but is not itself the product portfolio.
records.decision: Use Personal AI Harness as the name for the continuously evolving operating layer behind the work.
records.tradeoff: The name is less familiar than Portfolio OS, but it better describes the underlying agent and workflow infrastructure.
records.redaction_notes: Keep the explanation product-first and avoid exposing runtime mechanics.

records.title: Use one localized content model for English and Swedish
records.context: Recruiters may read the profile in either Swedish or English, while tag identifiers and evidence links must remain stable.
records.decision: Keep stable English tag IDs, add Swedish display labels, and require language-sync validation for profile changes.
records.tradeoff: A shared localized model costs more than an English-only page, but reduces translation drift.
records.redaction_notes: Present the user-facing language decision, not internal planning mechanics.

records.title: Test scheduled finding intake with a bounded canary first
records.context: A full cross-runtime reporting architecture would add cost before adoption and operator value were proven.
records.decision: Run a 14-day job-agent canary with one writer, one existing queue, deduplication, positive-evidence closure, and measured runtime cost.
records.tradeoff: The canary does not solve the final multi-producer architecture, but it lowers rollout risk and produces decision evidence.
evidence_refs: Shared harness plan: scheduled finding intake path decision, dated 2026-08-15
records.redaction_notes: Use the canary decision and evaluation logic without private tracker identifiers.

records.title: Keep reusable skill source runtime-neutral
records.context: A shared installer placed inside an upstream-managed runtime folder was lost during a system refresh, and a whole-root junction prevented runtime-specific adaptation.
records.decision: Move reusable installation logic to a shared source layer and expose skills per runtime, preserving local variants and rollback paths.
records.tradeoff: Per-skill synchronization is more explicit than one root junction, but it protects upgrades and supports multiple runtimes.
evidence_refs: Shared incident: shared skill installer runtime drift, dated 2026-08-10
records.redaction_notes: Remove machine paths, runtime internals, and credential details.

records.title: Separate product-code freshness from later documentation work
records.context: The latest commits combined a meaningful product-code milestone with later documentation and operations work.
records.decision: Name the latest product-code signal separately and avoid presenting every later commit as product progress.
records.tradeoff: The explanation is more precise, but it protects the credibility of the product narrative.
records.redaction_notes: Use only the already sanitized commit and evidence boundary.

records.title: Use committed source state and exclude dirty work in recruiter proof
records.context: The accessible source branch was committed, while newer local work remained uncommitted.
records.decision: Anchor recruiter-facing claims to the committed branch and label newer local work as outside the verified boundary.
records.tradeoff: Some recent work is not shown, but the published evidence remains reproducible.
records.redaction_notes: Do not include local worktree paths or private branch details.

records.title: Preserve the source repository handoff hierarchy
records.context: Orientation, durable status, and commit freshness are different kinds of truth in the lead product repository.
records.decision: Use orientation docs for navigation, durable status docs for product state, and direct source verification for freshness overrides.
records.tradeoff: The hierarchy requires more reading discipline, but avoids flattening different evidence types into one status claim.
records.redaction_notes: Link to public handoff documentation only.

records.title: Use direct source verification when status docs lag
records.context: A product can move faster than its curated status summary.
records.decision: Use status docs as context, but let direct git and file verification override stale freshness dates.
records.tradeoff: The weekly process needs extra verification, but published status remains current and defensible.
records.redaction_notes: Keep source references at the repository documentation level.

records.title: Show workflow improvements as supporting cases
records.context: Practical improvements were scattered across lessons, prompts, skills, automations, and templates.
records.decision: Create supporting workflow cases while keeping concrete product projects as the primary proof.
records.tradeoff: The operating layer becomes visible without allowing it to overshadow product execution.
records.redaction_notes: Use sanitized workflow cases, never raw prompts or local runtime details.

records.title: Keep concrete products ahead of the operating layer
records.context: The portfolio contains both product work and a substantial AI-native operating layer.
records.decision: Lead with Job-agent, use PKM and the household budget app as supporting products, and present automation as the enabling layer.
records.tradeoff: The harness receives less prominence, but the portfolio is easier to evaluate as product work.
records.redaction_notes: Keep product projects as the lead reading path.

records.title: Keep PKM supporting until sustained value is validated
records.context: The PKM work is promising, but sustained daily-use value needs stronger evidence.
records.decision: Present PKM as supporting evidence rather than claim validated product-market value.
records.tradeoff: The story is narrower, but it avoids overstating adoption or outcomes.
records.redaction_notes: Do not infer usage metrics that are not directly evidenced.

records.title: Use household budgeting as shared-domain modeling evidence
records.context: The budget app involves shared roles, imports, review flows, forecasts, and privacy-sensitive data.
records.decision: Present it as evidence of domain modeling and shared workflow design, not as a generic finance app claim.
records.tradeoff: The framing is more specific, but it makes the product reasoning easier to evaluate.
records.redaction_notes: Exclude private household details and personal financial data.

records.title: Keep repo-owned durable documents with the owning repository
records.context: Shared runtime documentation and product-repository documentation have different ownership and portability needs.
records.decision: Keep repo-specific plans, specs, reports, incidents, and runbooks in the owning repo, while reserving shared agent docs for cross-runtime coordination.
records.tradeoff: This creates clearer ownership and portability, but requires an explicit ownership check before writing a durable document.
evidence_refs: Shared lesson: repo docs stay with the owning repository, dated 2026-06-25
records.redaction_notes: Describe the ownership principle without exposing machine paths or runtime structure.

records.title: Make decision-heavy reports decision-first
records.context: A technically complete report can still be hard to act on if the actual decisions are buried in prose.
records.decision: Put counts, recommended actions, decision items, reply codes, and concise evidence near the top of decision-oriented reports.
records.tradeoff: The format gives less space to background before the decision, but improves speed and clarity for the reader.
evidence_refs: Shared lesson: decision-first report format, dated 2026-06-24
records.redaction_notes: Use the report-design principle without exposing internal task mechanics.
